To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the replicating DNA vaccines carrying HIV B'/C subtypes gag, pol, gp160, tat and nef can induce both humoral and cellular immune response.

(1) HIV B'/C subtypes gag, gp160, rtn genes can be efficiently expressed in replicating DNA vaccine vectors; (2) single-gene expression vector has the higher gene expression and induces stronger immunity; (3) combined inoculation of DNA vaccines containing Gagpol and gp160 genes has dramatically lower immunity than separate inoculation of Gp160 and Gagpol vaccines.
HIV B'/C subtypes gag, pol, gp160 and rt-n can be expressed in the DNA vaccines and induce cellular and humoral immunity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the gene expression and immune responses of HIV B'/ C subtype genes in replicating vector pSCK.
the effect of gene structures of HIV-1 B'/C subtype gene on expression and immunity in replicating DNA vaccine.
the effect of gene structures and immunization methods on expression of HIV B'/ C subtype genes and immunity in replicating DNA vaccine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the replicating DNA vaccines with HIV genes gag, pol and rtn can be efficiently expressed in pSCK2 vector, but the immune responses induced by them need further optimization.
the replicating DNA vectors are a good candidate for the construction of multi-HIV subtype genes vaccine.

the replicating DNA vector can efficiently express HIV B'/C genes, and the single-gene expression DNA plasmid has the higher gene expression and induces stronger immune response.
